title: Hardware Stencil Masking & Picture-in-Picture Zoom Views Architecture

blocks.content: Engineering notebook from `docs/STENCIL_MASKING_AND_ZOOM_VIEW_ARCHITECTURE.md`. This archive preserves the project’s original rationale, equations, performance reports and illustrative code. Historical paths, API names, claims and sketches can differ from the current engine. For copy-ready programs use the guides and demos; for current callable signatures use the source-derived API. Performance figures here describe reported experiments, not guaranteed frame rates.

blocks.text: Original document: [docs/STENCIL_MASKING_AND_ZOOM_VIEW_ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/docs/STENCIL_MASKING_AND_ZOOM_VIEW_ARCHITECTURE.md). See [current limitations](/limitations) for concrete compatibility notes.

Visual presentations frequently require clipping content to complex geometric boundaries (circular avatars, animated wipe masks, aperture cutouts) and magnifying focal details (technical zoom callouts, picture-in-picture insets).
Retiam provides three specialized layout entities:

items: **[`Mask`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/layout/Mask.ts)**: Hardware-accelerated stencil clipping using the 8-bit WebGPU stencil buffer (`depth24plus-stencil8`), supporting nested masks, inverted hole punching, and zero color-buffer pollution.

**[`ZoomView`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/layout/ZoomView.ts)**: Picture-in-picture magnifying callout that renders a target entity hierarchy into a focused circular or rectangular window with callout connector lines.

**[`FeedbackZoomView`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/layout/FeedbackZoomView.ts)**: High-performance frame-feedback alternative that samples the previous frame's rendered color buffer directly without cloning entity hierarchies, guaranteeing 100% fidelity with 3D models, video textures, and post-processed shaders.

blocks.text: The `Mask` entity accepts a boundary shape ([`VectorEntity`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/VectorEntity.ts)) and arbitrary target content ([`Entity`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/Entity.ts)):

blocks.code: new Mask(shape: VectorEntity, content: Entity, inverted: boolean = false)

blocks.text: Retiam partitions the 8-bit hardware stencil buffer (`0x00 - 0xFF`):

items: **Bits 0–6 (`0x01 - 0x7F`)**: Unique stencil mask ID ($1 \le \text{maskId} \le 127$). This allows up to 127 independent or nested masks to coexist without state cross-talk.

blocks.text: `Mask` automatically patches the depth-stencil states of child [`FragmentComponent`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/components/FragmentComponent.ts) instances:

children: **`writeMask = 0`**: Suppresses all RGBA color writes to the swap chain, rendering the mask boundary completely invisible.
**Stencil Operation**: `stencil.passOp = 'replace'`, writing `128 | maskId` into the stencil buffer wherever the shape's fill geometry exists.
**Normal Mask (`inverted: false`)**: `stencil.compare = 'equal'`, with reference value `128 | maskId`. Pixels outside the mask boundary fail the stencil test and are discarded.
**Inverted Mask (`inverted: true`)**: `stencil.compare = 'not-equal'`. Pixels inside the boundary are punched out, creating transparent holes.
